name: Categories and stages
summary: Defines what work is tracked (categories, such as drywall) and the measured steps within it (stages, such as framing or finish), including measurement formulas, order, colour and planned timelines.

roles.note: The matrix reflects seed data and role naming, not verified deployed assignments (DEC-010).

nfr.statement: Maximum categories per project and stages per category that configuration screens and recalculation must support.
nfr.open_question: What are the largest current projects, and what do we commit to? Needs product input plus production data.

requirements.title: Stages are tracked independently, without weighting
requirements.statement: Each stage within a category has its own progress. The system does not combine stages into one weighted category percentage (for example, framing 80% and paint 30% are not reported as walls 55%).

sources.title: Track3D "Single Source of Truth" docs, generated from code

acceptance_criteria.given: A category with stages Framing at 80% and Paint at 30% for one location
acceptance_criteria.when: A user views progress for that category
acceptance_criteria.then: Framing and Paint are shown as separate values, and no combined category percentage is calculated

requirements.title: Stage names, order and colours are unique within a category
requirements.statement: Within one category, no two stages may share a name, sequence position or colour. Stages are ordered by sequence.

acceptance_criteria.given: A category with a stage named Framing at sequence 1
acceptance_criteria.when: A user renames another stage to Framing, or moves it to sequence 1
acceptance_criteria.then: The change is rejected and the existing stages are unchanged

requirements.title: A category is active while any of its stages is active
requirements.statement: When every stage in a category is inactive, the category becomes inactive. Reactivating any stage reactivates the category. Inactive categories are left out of progress views.

acceptance_criteria.given: An active category with two active stages
acceptance_criteria.then: The category becomes inactive and disappears from customer progress views

acceptance_criteria.given: An inactive category whose stages are all inactive

requirements.title: Only category name and colour changes are audited
requirements.statement: Today, changes to a category's name and colour are written to the audit history. Changes to other configuration, such as formulas, units or stage order, are not shown to be audited.
requirements.rationale: Recorded so product can decide what configuration history is required (DEC-002).

acceptance_criteria.when: Its name or colour is changed
acceptance_criteria.then: The audit history records the previous and new value
